title: Unique Identifier Exposure
description: The video management service links child user data to the parent service via a unique identifier (e.g., user ID, session token). This allows the parent service to uniquely identify the child user, enabling potential linkage attacks or profiling.

title: Processing of Identified Information
description: The system processes video data that is identified information (e.g., user ID, session token). This processing enables the system to track and identify the child user.

title: Pseudonym Identification
description: The video data contains pseudonyms or identifiers (e.g., user ID) that uniquely reference the identity of the child data subject. This allows the system to identify the individual.

title: Observed Communications
description: The system observes communications between the parent service and the child user (e.g., API calls, data transfers). This observation enables the system to detect and track the flow of video data.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The system collects and processes video data of a highly sensitive type (e.g., personal video content). This data type is not functionally required for the basic service and is unnecessarily exposed.

title: Excessive Volume
description: The system processes a large volume of video data beyond what is functionally needed for the child user's basic access. This excessive volume increases the risk of data leakage.

title: Propagation
description: Processed video data is propagated to other services or external parties (e.g., analytics, marketing) where it is not strictly necessary for the child user's service.

title: Unlawful Processing
description: The processing of video data may not be lawful, potentially violating privacy regulations such as GDPR regarding the processing of personal data without a valid legal basis.

title: Sensitive Data Collection
description: The MongoDB childprofiles collection contains browsing data which is highly sensitive personal data. Collecting this data without a strict functional necessity for the AI recommendation engine creates a significant privacy risk.

title: Granular Data Collection
description: The childprofiles collection contains granular browsing data (e.g., specific pages visited, timestamps, device info) which is more fine-grained than functionally needed for the AI recommendation engine.

title: Excessive Processing
description: The browsing data is being processed and potentially enriched or transformed for the AI recommendation engine, which may be unnecessary for the core recommendation functionality.

title: Data Propagation
description: The browsing data is accessible by or propagated to other services where it is not strictly needed for the AI recommendation engine.

title: Excessive Exposure
description: The browsing data is made accessible to the AI recommendation engine, which is a known and anticipated party, potentially amplifying the risk of data exposure.

title: Sensitive Data Collection
description: The AI Recommendation Engine processes the childprofiles data, which is highly sensitive personal data. Processing this data without a strict functional necessity creates a significant privacy risk.

title: Granular Data Collection
description: The AI Recommendation Engine processes granular browsing data (e.g., specific pages visited, timestamps, device info) which is more fine-grained than functionally needed for the AI recommendation engine.

title: Excessive Processing
description: The browsing data is being processed and potentially enriched or transformed for the AI recommendation engine, which may be unnecessary for the core recommendation functionality.

title: Data Propagation

title: Excessive Exposure
description: The browsing data is made accessible to the AI recommendation engine, which is a known and anticipated party, potentially amplifying the risk of data exposure.

title: Sensitive Data Collection
description: AI Recommendation Engine collects browsing data (e.g., location, search history, device info) which is highly sensitive and not functionally required for the recommendation algorithm.

title: Granular Data Collection
description: The system collects browsing data at a fine-grained level (e.g., individual page views, specific search terms) which is more detailed than necessary for the recommendation engine.

title: Excessive Processing
description: The system processes browsing data for analysis and enrichment beyond what is strictly necessary to generate the recommendation.

title: Exposure to Third-Party Parties
description: Browsing data is made accessible to Third-Party Advertisers (EE3), which is a predetermined set of parties known at design time but represents a significant amplification of data exposure compared to a closed internal system.

title: Implicit Data Disclosure
description: Browsing data is implicitly collected as a side-effect of the data flow to advertisers, even if the user does not explicitly consent to the specific data being sent.

title: Unique Identifier Linking
description: The authentication service (P1) links to the file system (DS4) using a unique identifier (e.g., government ID number). This allows the system to associate the data flow with a specific individual, enabling linking of data across the flow.
assumptions: The government ID is a unique identifier within the system.

title: Processing of Identified Data
description: The authentication service (P1) processes identified data (the government ID) as part of the authentication process. This is a direct request and processing of personal data.
assumptions: The government ID is personal data.

title: Identifier in Data
description: The authentication service (P1) processes data that contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject (the government ID). This is a direct processing of identifiable information.
assumptions: The government ID is identifiable information.

title: Observed Communications
description: The authentication service (P1) observes communications between the user and the file system (DS4) as part of the authentication process. This is a direct observation of data flow.
assumptions: The communication is observed by the system.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The authentication service (P1) collects and processes highly sensitive data (government ID images) which should only be collected and processed when strictly required. This is a direct processing of sensitive data.
assumptions: Government ID images are highly sensitive data.

title: Data Type Granularity
description: The authentication service (P1) discloses personal data of a more fine-grained level of granularity than functionally needed. The images are processed at a level of detail that may be excessive.
assumptions: The granularity of the images is more fine-grained than functionally needed.

title: Treatment, Analysis, Enrichment
description: The authentication service (P1) processes the government ID images for authentication purposes, which involves treatment, analysis, and enrichment of the data beyond what is strictly required for the basic authentication function.
assumptions: Authentication requires analysis and enrichment of the ID images.

title: Implicit Data Disclosure
description: The authentication service (P1) implicitly collects the government ID images as a side-effect of the authentication process, even if the user does not explicitly request the images.
assumptions: The system collects the ID images as a side-effect of the authentication flow.

title: Predetermined Set of Parties
description: The authentication service (P1) makes the government ID images accessible to a predetermined set of parties (the file system backend) which is static and fixed. This is a direct disclosure to a known, limited set of parties.
assumptions: The file system is a known, static party.

title: Availability/Accessibility of Data
description: The authentication service (P1) publishes or broadcasts the government ID images to the file system backend, making them accessible to the system. This amplifies the potential risk of data exposure.
assumptions: The images are published to the backend.

title: Unawareness as Data Subject
description: The user (data subject) may be unaware that their government ID images are being collected, processed, stored, or disclosed by the authentication service (P1) for authentication purposes.
assumptions: The user may not be aware of the data flow.

title: Preferences
description: The user (data subject) may lack control over how their government ID images are processed, stored, or disclosed by the authentication service (P1).
assumptions: The user may not have control over the processing.

title: Access
description: The user (data subject) may lack control in accessing the government ID images that are being processed by the authentication service (P1).
assumptions: The user may not have access to the images.

title: Rectification/Erasure
description: The user (data subject) may lack control in rectifying incorrect data or removing government ID images that are no longer relevant to the authentication process.
assumptions: The user may not have control over data removal.

title: Invalid Consent
description: The authentication service (P1) may rely on invalid consent for the processing of government ID images, as the consent may not be valid or the lawfulness of the processing is questionable.
assumptions: Consent may be invalid or the lawfulness is questionable.

title: Violation of Storage Limitation Principle
description: The authentication service (P1) may store government ID images for longer than functionally needed, potentially violating the storage limitation principle.
assumptions: Images may be stored longer than necessary.

title: Improper Personal Data Management
description: The authentication service (P1) may involve improper personal data management practices, such as inadequate security or management of the data flow.
assumptions: Security or management practices may be inadequate.

title: Insufficient Cybersecurity Risk Management
description: The authentication service (P1) may lack proper cybersecurity risk management with specific attention to the interplay with privacy risks.
assumptions: Cybersecurity risk management may be insufficient.

title: Data Propagation
description: JWT data is stored in localStorage and accessible to the browser, potentially allowing it to be accessed by other services or users not intended to process it.

title: Implicit Data Disclosure
description: The JWT is stored in localStorage, which is a data store accessible to the browser. This constitutes implicit disclosure of the JWT to the browser context.

title: Duration/Retention
description: The JWT is stored in localStorage indefinitely, which may exceed the functional retention period required for authentication.

title: Involved Parties
description: The JWT is stored in localStorage, which is accessible to the browser. This exposes the JWT to the browser context, which may be a party not intended to process it.

title: Availability/Accessibility
description: The JWT is stored in localStorage, which is accessible to the browser. This exposes the JWT to the browser context, which may be a party not intended to process it.
